# M0 build spec — kernel, bent cut, fusion, determinism and site spikes (risk retirement)

Lane `build/m0-spec`. Written 2026-10-03 on the owner's Mac — §12.1's reference machine — by the Fable seat that
continued the cloud seat's work (ledger rows L-0001, L-0002 in `plat/CLEAN-ROOM.md`). The design is a REFERENCE, NOT A
CONTRACT (J156): where it is unclear or leaves a case open, the builder picks, records the pick in
`plat/docs/build/choices.md` and the tests judge; tangled features are STAGED (the basic case first, the rest named with
its milestone); no new design is added. Every section pointer below is to `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. The machine-readable
twin of §2 is `plat/docs/build/M0-work.json` (one object per work item; the authority where the two differ).

---

## 0 Standing rules, the machine, and the Mac corrections

### 0.1 The owner's standing rules for the build (J156, J157)

1. **Design = reference.** A choice where the design is unclear is one row of `choices.md` (id, date, seat, section,
   choice, reason, the test that holds it); rows are append-only; a reversal is a new row naming the row it supersedes.
2. **Staging.** M0 builds each piece's basic case and names what it defers and to which milestone (§4b).
3. **No new design.** A scope line stands until M1.
4. **The machine.** The reference machine of §12.1 itself (facts in 0.2). pnpm is never global: every command is
   `corepack pnpm …` (C-0030).
5. **Timings.** A timing taken in §12.1's timing phase on this machine — otherwise idle, on AC power, after 30 s idle,
   batches ≤ 60 s, `bench/calibrate` before and after within 5 % — is **AUTHORITATIVE**; one taken while other seats run
   is **CONTENDED** and never gates (C-0025, C-0047). Timing bars run in a wave of their own with nothing else running.
6. **Disk.** The data volume has ≈ 2.6 GB free: one pnpm store (the default), no git worktrees, bench and log output to
   `/private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-cstokes-Desktop-Maps/2367ceda-b0ec-4fa5-94a3-059f82e2d4b7/scratchpad/build/`
   (`PLAT_BENCH_OUT`), truncated by the harness; no browser download beyond the cached builds (C-0028); a seat that sees
   under 1 GB free (`df -h /Users/cstokes`) stops and reports.
7. **M-1 runs beside M0** in its research-side lane. A piece that needs the reference recordings or M-1's baselines is
   **AFTER-M-1**: scheduled in the wave that starts when `plat/packages/testkit/baselines/baselines.json`, the digest
   `plat/docs/digest/` and `ng-faces.json` (C-0043) are committed; never parked, faked or estimated (§1's lists name every
   row and digest entry needed).
8. **Clean room (§17.1 (1)).** Implementer-side seats read only `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/volumes/INDEX.md`, the
   volumes a milestone builds (M0: none), `plat/` and `plat/docs/digest/`, published papers and the public documentation
   of adopted libraries. On this machine the whole reference corpus is present, so the firewall is physical: every
   search, find, grep, du or ls runs inside `plat/` or on a named design file — never recursively from the project root
   or `docs/` — and never follows a symbolic link out of `plat/`. Every seat signs `plat/CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2 before its
   work lands (its row: seat, date, role, what it read).
9. **Working rules for every seat.** Save as you go; a CHECKPOINT line in `docs/lane-events.log` at least every twenty
   minutes; a LANDED line with the files when complete; long command output to the scratchpad build directory; commit
   and push nothing (the session commits).

### 0.2 The machine (probed 2026-10-03; receipts in the lane log)

MacBookAir10,1 (fanless), Apple M1 — 4 performance + 4 efficiency cores — 16 GB, macOS 14.7.8 (23H730); Node 24.12.0
arm64 (V8 13.6.233.17) as a universal binary whose x86_64 slice runs under Rosetta 2 as a genuine x64 V8
(`arch -x86_64 node` → `process.arch` `x64`, same version and V8); npm 11.6; corepack 0.34.5; Apple clang 16.0.0
(arm64; `-arch x86_64` cross-compiles, `arch -x86_64` runs it); no `pnpm` on PATH; Playwright cache at
`~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright`: chromium 1223 and 1243 (with their headless shells), firefox 1522, webkit
`mac14_arm64_special` 2251; outbound HTTP 200 from `registry.npmjs.org`, `nodejs.org`, `www.netlib.org/fdlibm/` and
`prng.di.unimi.it` (the Playwright CDN answers but is not used); on AC power; 2.6 GB free of 228 GB.

## 1 Scope — M0's pieces (a)–(f): now, AFTER-M-1, and the timing bars

Legend: **NOW** = built and judged on this machine in M0's waves; **TIMING** = a bar measured in the timing-phase wave
(M0-t-01) by §12.1's protocol; **AFTER-M-1** = needs the reference recordings or M-1's baselines, with exactly what it
needs. "Here" in §2's bar lists means NOW.

### (a) `@plat/kernel` (§3, §2.2) — NOW
Lattice, snapping, exact predicates, one arena per layer with the five levels as views, role and owner tables and
reference resolution, attraction and contact semantics, batched transactions with stage-end index partitions, booleans /
buffers / bands on the arrangement with the CI oracles, OBB / hull / LIR / regular fit, snap rounding, the straight
skeleton with its validator and exact OBB roofs, the sampled medial axis, warp and smoothing, the invariant suite, the
arena block (C-0037) and the façade. Items M0-a-01 … M0-a-16.
* Bars NOW: B-FUZZ 0 crashes / hangs / invalid outputs on 10⁶ random inputs per primitive and on M0's constructive set
  (C-0038; §13.1); §3.7 (i)'s differential oracle agreement (unattracted: equal face counts and symmetric difference
  ≤ perimeter × 1 cm; attracted: valid and ≤ perimeter × √2 · `attractCm`; ≥ 10⁵ unattracted cases per operation);
  §3.8's fixture bar (0 crashes, 0 validator failures); the corpus bar (downgrades ≤ 0.5 %, work-limit hits ≤ 0.1 %) on
  the stand-in corpus (C-0015), re-run on B-CITY-lite at M1; op-order determinism and slot-renumbering identity (§13.2);
  save → load → save byte-identical on the arena block.
* Bars TIMING: insert + snap + attract + re-walk ≤ 8 µs per growth proposal; `splitFace` per bent cut against §12.4's
  S8 row (≈ 12 µs); §3.7 (ii): S9's corridor bands over the CITY face set against §12.4's S9 row (25 ms) and one
  district ≤ 3 ms; S11's geometry share ≤ 3 µs per plot median on a synthetic per-plot workload (the kernel calls §3.7
  names; re-measured at M1 on B-CITY-lite's S11); skeleton ≤ 20 µs median per footprint. A miss takes §3.7's rule
  (one optimisation pass; > 2× → the WebAssembly accelerator for that loop; ≤ 2× → the measured cost carried into
  §12.4's row or a declared budget amendment), recorded in the M0 record (C-0026).
* AFTER-M-1: none.

### (b) The bent-cut transaction with the hole slit (§4.6; items 34–41) — NOW, comparison AFTER-M-1
The planner (steps 1–7), the transaction with its ladder (step 8), width (9), continuation (10), recursion (11), the
deep-interior rule and the seam portals. Items M0-b-01 … M0-b-04; AFTER-M-1 M0-b-05.
* Bars NOW: T34-1, T36-1, T37-1, T38-1's shape clauses, T39-1, T40-1, T41-1 on the M0 (b) synthetic face set (curved,
  round-joined, triangular, C-shaped and holed faces) in the PR tier, T34-1's 10 000-face mean (`g` within 7/30 ± 3
  s.e.) nightly; F-CUT's bars: on 10⁵ random concave and holed faces the ladder ends in ≤ 6 kernel calls, the face count
  never decreases, each district's substitution residue ≤ 5 % (soft); 0 lanes cross a wall strip.
* Bars TIMING: `splitFace` per cut (above).
* **AFTER-M-1** (M0-b-05; exactly these inputs): (1) `baselines.json` rows of §13.5's **bent-cut signature** —
  σ plain 0.066 and ring 0.098 (±0.02), the corner-within-0.10-of-mid-course share (≥ 80 %), the ≥ 85° arrival share
  (≥ 95 %), the fillet share on identical face shapes (±0.05) — each with `referenceBuild` NG 1.2.2 and
  `metricVersion`; (2) §13.5's **blocks** row (NG block counts per template at `medium`) for the block-area and
  cut-length KS by the band rule; (3) **`ng-faces.json`** (C-0043): NG's recorded face shapes as integer-centimetre
  rings by template with each face's recorded numbers; (4) the re-fitted plot-depth rows and regime block-depth
  minimums (item 34, J-A34.01) as cells for `granularity.json` and `regimes.json`, provenance "M-1 ⟨date⟩"; (5) digest
  entries: how NG's σ was measured (the recorded frame, the rotated retries included), the hollow-block frequency's
  definition, the junction census (T versus crossroads). From these M0-b-05 runs T34-1 – T41-1 and §13.5's signature row
  on NG's shapes, calibrates `cut.flattenM` (J-A37.01) and applies the depth rows. The comparison is **the check of
  the adopted corner-first rule** (§16).

### (c) The fused-layout spike — S4 routing + S5 growth + S8 infill on a flat synthetic site at CITY face counts (§4.3, §4.4, §4.6) — NOW, statistics AFTER-M-1
The flat fixture with its S3 slice (C-0016, C-0032), the trace strategy with the strip stand-in (C-0033), S4, S5a–S5d,
S8 through (b), and the gate harness. Items M0-c-01 … M0-c-06; AFTER-M-1 M0-c-07.
* Bars NOW: no turn cliff (10 m resampling: no empty bin above 15° while the bin below holds > 1 %); junction p5 ≥ 30°;
  0 whole-map restarts on 1 000 seeds (the pipeline has no restart path; the harness asserts the report carries none
  and counts every ladder use); the growth-drift row (net turn over 600 m p50 15–30°, > 90° on ≤ 1 %); the face-count
  report (≈ 1 500 cuts, ≈ 25 districts at CITY, §12.4); roads leaving the walled stage = N.
* Bars TIMING: S4 + S5 + S8 ≤ 100 ms at CITY. A miss: extramural growth stops at `secondary` (lanes infill-only
  everywhere, a switch built at M0) and the gate re-runs (§4.4).
* **AFTER-M-1** (M0-c-07): the block-area and junction-degree distributions inside the NG bands **on the same district
  shapes** — §13.5's blocks row and junction row (NG 361 / 361 T; the 4-way share), with NG's hood outlines carried in
  `ng-faces.json`; the **MFCG street-signature rows** (R4 at 60 / 120 / 250 m, wall alignment by distance band, T / Y
  share, intramural dead ends, blocks per ha, lots per block ⟨M-1⟩) by the band rule; the deep-interior row (NG
  hollow-block frequency, MFCG inner-lot removal ⟨M-1⟩) and the fitted default shares of §4.6's deep-interior rule;
  the digest's confirmation of R4's definition (C-0018, `metricVersion`). A statistics miss: the infill constants
  recalibrated against those rows before M1 (§4.4).

### (d) The determinism spike (§6) — NOW
Structured stream keys, lineage-hash minting, the Merkle digest with the kernel's level digests, `dmath`, the
time-dilation shim, the allowlist lint with its vendored scan, the matching routine, the cross-host harness. Items
M0-d-01 … M0-d-09, M0-m-01.
* Bars NOW: digests identical on Node arm64, Node x64 (Rosetta), Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, workers on and off, 100
  seeds of the spike city (C-0028); every stream key and lineage hash distinct in the spike city (the sky-island clause
  at M6-sky); time dilation byte-identical; op-order determinism; the known-answer tests of xoshiro128\*\*, MurmurHash3
  (SMHasher 0xB3ECE62A; `H32` check vectors of §13.6 (2)) and `dmath` on both architectures; a full root recomputation
  equals the maintained root after every batch (the CI oracle).
* Bars TIMING: ≤ 0.1 µs per structured key; digest maintenance ≤ 5 % of each batch's own time at CITY; root
  finalisation ≤ 5 ms at a stage end; full recomputation ≤ 150 ms at CITY, the records tree (synthetic, C-0015)
  included; matching ≤ 2 µs per point-anchored and ≤ 20 µs per overlap-anchored entity. Each has §6.2's / §6.3's
  pre-decided fallback, none of which moves a golden.
* AFTER-M-1: none.

### (e) The site-and-fields spike — S1 + S4 + S6 with §12.4's mechanisms (§4.2 S1, §4.3, §4.5) — NOW
S1 (1), (3), (5) basic, (8), (9), (10) basic (C-0048); S4 through (c); S6's perimeter, grower, typing stand-in
(C-0035), quarter tree and the three fields' pass 1 with `FieldBands` (C-0049). Items M0-e-01 … M0-e-06.
* Bars NOW: D8 defined on 100 % of the hydrology grid's land cells over frame and margin on 60 m and 3 000 m relief;
  the river's bed monotone to its outfall; carve ≤ `carveMaxCm`; the 3 000 m relief fixture stores without a clamp;
  containment 100 % by construction; the count law within ± 1; gate / bridgehead wards' median area below the town's on
  ≥ 90 % of seeds; `FieldBands` cuts give the shares' land within one cell; soft terms at weight 0 byte-identical.
* Bars TIMING: S1 + S4 + S6 ≤ 50 ms at CITY, or R12-5's coarsening (fields and margin 32 → 48 m; hydrology 25 → 32 m at
  CITY, 32 → 40 m at METROPOLIS, 16 → 20 m at TOWN — a switch built at M0) applied and re-measured.
* AFTER-M-1: none.

### (f) The CI tiers timed (§13.8) — NOW, budgets TIMING
`bench/calibrate`, the timing-phase protocol, the tiers as local scripts, the work-limit laws and their coefficients.
Items M0-f-01, M0-f-02, M0-f-03a, M0-f-03b.
* Bars TIMING: each tier inside its budget by C-0027's reading (PR ≤ 15 min on these 8 cores gates; nightly ≤ 4 h and
  milestone ≤ 12 h projected on 16 cores), or §13.8's fallback (B-CITY-lite 25 seeds — at M0 the spike runs — and random
  fuzz 5 × 10³ per primitive, the constructive set never cut) applied.
* NOW: the F-WORK coefficients from the spikes' measured 99.9th percentile per unit × 1.5 (C-0021), the hit-rate report.

### Timing bars, listed once (the timing-phase wave, M0-t-01)
insert ≤ 8 µs per proposal · `splitFace` ≈ 12 µs per cut · S9 bands one district ≤ 3 ms and the CITY set against 25 ms ·
S11 geometry share ≤ 3 µs per plot (synthetic) · skeleton ≤ 20 µs median · ≤ 0.1 µs per stream key · digest ≤ 5 % /
≤ 5 ms / ≤ 150 ms · matching ≤ 2 µs / ≤ 20 µs · fusion S4 + S5 + S8 ≤ 100 ms · site S1 + S4 + S6 ≤ 50 ms · the tiers'
budgets · the hydrology row (≈ 16 ms at CITY, reported) · the stand-in corpus skeleton rate.

## 2 The work breakdown

Sixty items in fifteen waves plus the timing-phase wave and the AFTER-M-1 wave; at most four implementer seats run at
once; the timing-phase wave runs alone. Each item is one seat's sitting of a few hours. No two items own one file: a
package's `src/index.ts`, `package.json` and `tsconfig.json` and the workspace files are the scaffold's (M0-s-01), each
module folder's `index.ts` starts empty and passes to the folder's owner (C-0013); `workLimits.json` is created by
M0-f-03a and handed to M0-f-03b (C-0021). Every item's tests live in its own folder (`*.test.ts`) and its fixtures under
`<package>/test/fixtures/<item>/`. The full field set per item (owned files, design sections, interfaces by the design's
names, tests, exit bars with their timing, dependencies, wave) is in `M0-work.json`; this table is its index.

| wave | seats | items |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | M0-s-01 scaffold |
| 1 | 4 | M0-a-01 numeric core · M0-d-02 MurmurHash3 · M0-d-03 dmath · M0-m-01 model types and records |

## 3 The check protocol — how a checker seat accepts an item

A checker seat is implementer-side (it signs `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §2 like every seat) and never the item's author.

1. **Read the brief whole.** The item in `M0-work.json`, its entry above, every design section it names (read in full,
   not skimmed), the `choices.md` rows it cites and any rows the author appended.
2. **Read the code whole.** Every file the item owns; confirm the diff stays inside them (`git diff --stat` against
   the item's `owns` list; a touched file outside it fails the item unless a choices row re-assigned ownership).
3. **Run the gates**, all as `corepack pnpm …`: `install --frozen-lockfile`; `lint` (the allowlist, dependency direction,
   path rule, vendored scan); `build` (`tsc -b`); `test --project <package>` and the item's own test files; the item's
   bars marked *here* in `M0-work.json` (B-FUZZ at the PR size for a kernel item; the harness for a spike item); a
   timing bar is NOT run by the checker (the timing-phase wave runs it) — the checker verifies the harness exists,
   emits the stamped record and refuses to gate on a `contended` result.
4. **The checklist** (each line pass or fail, quoted with evidence):
   * every interface the item lists is present under the design's name and signature (§3.4's list, §14's interfaces);
   * every test id the item lists is implemented and green; every design clause the item names has a test or a named
     reason it cannot have one yet (an AFTER-M-1 or deferred clause names its milestone);
   * **no undeclared shortcut**: a stub is a `notBuilt('<milestone>')` with a choices row or a §4b entry; a `TODO`,
     a skipped test without a milestone tag, a silently narrowed bar or a constant where a table cell is required fails;
   * **no undeclared deviation**: where the code departs from a design section, a `choices.md` row exists naming the
     section, the choice and the test; otherwise fail;
   * every table cell carries `unit`, `provenance` and `calibratable`; no `Math` member outside §6.5 (3)'s allowlist in
     a model package; no import, fixture or script path resolves outside `plat/`;
   * the author's `CLEAN-ROOM.md` row exists and lists what the author read; nothing it lists lies outside rule 1;
   * `bugs` empty in every run; no `contended` timing presented as a result.
5. **Verdict** written to `plat/docs/build/checks/<item id>.md`: pass or fail, each checklist line with its evidence
   (command and quoted output), every conclusion labelled CONFIRMED (executed) or PLAUSIBLE (reasoned), and the
   checker's ledger row. A failed item returns to its author with the failing lines; the fix round re-runs the failed
   lines and the item's whole test set. An item is LANDED only on a pass; the lane log carries both lines.

**Package rules (§14).** Dependency direction `kernel ← model ← tables ← {site} ← layout`; `testkit` may import every
package and is imported by nothing shipped; `bench` imports `testkit` and the packages; no model package has DOM types;
every adopted runtime library is imported in exactly one adapter file of the one package that uses it (`kernel/src/
adapters/{robust-predicates,flatbush,delaunator}.ts`, `site/src/adapters/simplex-noise.ts`); `exports` carry the
`plat-source` condition (C-0013). The lint enforces all of it (M0-d-07).

**Dev dependencies, pinned exactly (§17.4; registry on 2026-10-03):** typescript 6.0.3 (C-0014), typescript-eslint 8.71.0,
eslint 10.12.0, vitest 5.0.3, fast-check 4.10.2, esbuild 0.28.2, tsx 4.23.15, playwright-core at the release whose
browsers are the cached ones (C-0028; M0-s-01 records the exact number after confirming each cached revision launches),
clipper2-wasm 0.4.0 (BSL-1.0, oracle), polygon-clipping 0.15.7 (MIT, oracle). No prerelease in the production closure;
the licence checker runs over it in the PR tier.

**The lint of §6.5 (3) (M0-d-07).** In `kernel`, `model`, `tables`, `site`, `layout` (and every file whose output reaches
a digest): `Math` members only `abs floor ceil round trunc sign min max sqrt imul clz32 fround`; `**` forbidden
(C-0008); no `Math.random`, `Date`, `performance`, timers, `crypto.getRandomValues`, DOM, `toLocaleString`,
`localeCompare`, `Intl`; `Array.prototype.sort` only with a comparator; no `for…in`, `Object.keys/values/entries`
(C-0009; `Map` / `Set` insertion order allowed); the division rule (C-0044); the dependency direction; the repository
path rule with symbolic links resolved (§17.1 (3)); no bare `pnpm` in scripts (C-0030). The vendored scan is the same
`Math` census over `vendor/*/` with its report and the audit record.

**Commands** (the only forms documented): `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (with
`PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1`) · `corepack pnpm build` · `corepack pnpm test` · `corepack pnpm lint` ·
`corepack pnpm bench -- <harness>` · `corepack pnpm bench:calibrate` · `corepack pnpm bench:timing-phase` ·
`corepack pnpm tier:pr | tier:nightly | tier:milestone` · `corepack pnpm vendor:verify`.

**`plat/CLEAN-ROOM.md`** is written (rules at the top; ledger rows L-0001, L-0002; §5 for published sources).

## 5 Open questions the design leaves to M0 — decided (J122, J154)

1. **What is "a B-CITY city" before M1?** The spike city and schema-shaped synthetic records (C-0015); re-run at M1.
2. **Which of S3 do the spikes build?** The slice of C-0032 (lattice, picks, routes, `T`, level sets, gates, trace, the
   plaza); the rest M1.
3. **How does S8 meet a wall before S7 exists?** The strip stand-in of C-0033 — S7's own setback and glacis lines, laid
   by the trace strategy one milestone early, so no lane is planned through the band.
4. **What band does the fusion spike's S8 read without S6?** The synthetic ramp of C-0034, and the integrated run with
   S6's real pass-1 field reported beside it.
5. **How does S6 type without a roster?** The synthetic demand of C-0035.
6. **What does the substitution rung do without an allocation?** A `court` block, counted as residue (C-0036).
7. **Is §3.9 M0's or M1's?** The arena block is M0's (B-FUZZ's property and the renumbering test read it); the document
   is M1's (C-0037).
8. **Is "the whole constructive set" literally whole at M0?** No — by the design's own dates (§3.3's carve fixtures at
   M3a); M0 runs every class whose mechanism it builds and tags the rest with their milestones (C-0038).
9. **Which `dmath` routines?** Exactly those M0's code reads (C-0039); more as readers land.
10. **Which libraries are vendored at M0?** Four runtime libraries; no `flatqueue` (C-0040).
11. **Transient arenas now or later?** M6-P, with the types declared now (C-0041).
12. **What is M0's exit record?** `M0-record.md` + `M0-record.json` in §13.3's shape (C-0042).
13. **How do NG's recorded shapes reach the PR tier?** As `ng-faces.json`, a numbers-only crossing file M-1 delivers
    (C-0043); routed to the fix list.
14. **Which lints at M0?** The division rule yes, the unit lint at M1 with the schemas (C-0044).
15. **How much of `ChainProfile` at M0?** Reading, cutting and joining; the Write protocol at M2b (C-0045).
16. **How is a timing's standing decided?** By measurement, never by declaration (C-0047).
17. **How much of S1 at M0?** Terrain, hydrology, the river, basic crossing sites, water faces, outfalls, basic resources
    (C-0048).
18. **Where do `FieldBands`' shares come from before S2?** The band set's default household shares (C-0049).
19. **Which Node runs the x86 leg?** The universal binary's x86_64 slice under Rosetta 2 (C-0028); no download.
20. **Which Playwright?** `playwright-core` at the release whose cached builds match (C-0028); the WebKit leg uses the
    cached `mac14_arm64_special` build, which Playwright itself substitutes on macOS 14. Should any cached browser
    refuse to launch under the pinned release, that leg is reported blocked by the owner's no-download rule and the
    one download (≈ 100 MB) is asked of the owner — never faked.
21. **Where does `plat/` live?** In the Maps repository until the owner names its host (C-0031).
22. **How are the 16-core tier budgets judged on 8 cores?** Projected from CPU time (C-0027) until a runner exists.
23. **How does the `Seam` record look before II.1?** Minimal, with portals (C-0046).
24. **Where does the §3.7 "S11 geometry share" bar run without S11?** On a synthetic per-plot workload of the kernel
    calls §3.7 names; re-measured at M1 (§1 (a)).
25. **Which stage registers which `txForm` at M0?** As §4.1 states: callback for S5c and S8; declared for S3's slice, S4,
    S5a, S5b; S1 and S6 callback ("always safe").

Nothing is left open.

## 7 CONFIRMED versus PLAUSIBLE

**CONFIRMED (executed on 2026-10-03):** the machine facts of 0.2 (`sysctl`, `sw_vers`, `node -p`, `arch -x86_64 node -p
process.arch` → `x64`, `clang --version`, `which pnpm` → none, the Playwright cache listing, `pmset`, `df`); the egress
probes (HTTP HEAD, no content); the registry's `latest` versions and licences of the dev and vendored libraries and the
`browsers.json` of `playwright-core` 1.52.0 – 1.63.0; that M0.md and M0-work.json did not exist and no LANDED line stood
for this lane. **PLAUSIBLE (reasoned):** the wave plan's seat-hours; that the cached WebKit special build launches under
the pinned `playwright-core` (M0-s-01 confirms, §5 item 20); every budget and bar until the timing phase runs.
